--- title: "Initial and final syllable deletion" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_INICIAL_Y_FINAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_INICIAL_Y_FINAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Supresión de la sílaba inicial y final*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_INICIAL_Y_FINAL.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Initial and final syllable deletion, at age 5 (1,139 administrations in 2 cohorts). AUC .72 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1746 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 10 (1746) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | El alumno o alumna partirá de una palabra a la que se le quitará sílabas en diferentes posiciones para que quede una palabra nueva. Hay un total de 10 items: 5 de supresión de sílaba inicial, 5 de supresión de sílaba final. *(Spanish)* | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 28/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 1746|Supresión sílaba Inicial y final |Un dibujo o lámina por pantalla | 10| 2|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 5| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1746.** 2 de entrenamiento + 10 (5 de sílaba inicial y 5 de final). La lámina se corta en pantallas estrechas. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1746 · Supresión sílaba Inicial y final](../../figuras/plataforma/1746.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1746"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](../CF523.en.qmd) and [rapid naming](../RAN.en.qmd). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.1| 2014| 896|2019/20 | 350| 13| 337| 22| | 5.2| 2010| 130|2015/16 | 789| 257| 531| 35| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 5.2| 257| 2010| 7.03| 4.50| 8| -0.24| 8.17| 28.40| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 5.2| 257|0–12 |0–12 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .28–.68. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Letter knowledge (5.1, r = .40); Oral morphosyntax (5.2, r = .39). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .72. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .60–.61. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_INICIAL_Y_FINAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .62 (1 time point; 203–203 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 5.1| 350| 2014| 1| 2| 3| 5| 8| 11| 12| | 5.2| 257| 2010| 0| 1| 1| 2| 8| 12| 12| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_INICIAL_Y_FINAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 325| 0.262| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 320| 0.052| 0.646| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 337| 0.127| 0.020| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 350| 0.234| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 789| 0.130| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 752| -0.119| 0.104| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 751| 0.067| 0.066| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 789| 0.190| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Initial and final syllable deletion” (code 1746; LEEDUCA battery) assesses syllable awareness (deletion). Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 2 sessions, from 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .60–.61. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 5.2 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
